claims.claim: Hesychius of Jerusalem was a Christian priest (πρεσβύτερος) of Jerusalem.
Hesychius of Jerusalem was active during the first half of the fifth century, probably dying around 450.
Hesychius served as a priest in the church in Jerusalem around 412 and was recognized by 429 as the pre-eminent biblical interpreter and teacher of the church in Jerusalem and Palestine.
Hesychius of Jerusalem composed Homily 16, On the Conception of John the Baptist, which he preached during John's feast in Jerusalem.
The homily was written in Greek at Jerusalem in the early 5th century.

The homily covers the mission of the prophets, John's role as prophet, praise of Elisabeth, praise of John, the annunciation to Zachariah and John's birth, John's asceticism, the Baptism of Christ, and John's conflict with Herod and beheading.
Hesychius was renowned as a preacher and theologian in the Eastern Church.
Hesychius was acclaimed as having annotated the whole of sacred Scripture.
Hesychius played a prominent role in the 5th-century controversy on the nature of Christ and was a strong opponent of Nestorianism.
Hesychius is credited with the earliest known liturgical addresses on the Virgin Mary.
Hesychius must not be confused with Bishop Hesychius of Jerusalem, a contemporary of Gregory the Great.
